raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I'm sitting here at the start of the season, same as every year for thirty-odd years now...

---

**How I'm thinking about this year**

I've got 10.9 mu. Not a lot, but it's mine to work. Eight mouths at home — me, my wife, my son and his wife, their two kids, and my old mother still with us, plus my younger son who comes back between jobs in the city. Two of the boys work outside, they send some cash back, which helps. But the land still has to feed us and put cash in my pocket.

I split it up like this — **about 6 mu for cotton, and the other 4.9 mu for wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same ground.** Cotton is the money crop, that's what pays. Wheat and maize, that's what we eat and what feeds the chickens and the pig.

I never went to school. I just do what I know, what my father showed me, what works on my land. Fancy calculations and soil tests — that's for the business farms. I watch the weather, I watch my neighbors, I watch the fields.

---

**Cotton (6 mu) — my cash crop**

I plant around Guyu (late April), after the cold is gone. I buy the improved seed from the shop in town, maybe 25 yuan a mu worth. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — about **two bags (100 jin = 50 kg) of 15-15-15 compound across 6 mu**, so roughly 17 kg a mu at the base. Then when it flowers in July I'll topdress with urea, one bag over the cotton patch, that's maybe 8 kg urea per mu. All told, around 12-13 kg of nitrogen a mu. I don't measure — I just know, two bags base, one bag top. Same as always.

Bollworm and aphids will come. I'll spray 4 or 5 times through the season with whatever the shop has that's not too expensive. Also a pre-emergent herbicide early on, otherwise the weeds choke the rows.

I'll water twice from the well — once after planting to set them, once in flowering if July stays dry. Electricity for the pump isn't free, can't be watering for nothing.

Picking — all by hand. Me, my wife, and my daughter-in-law when she's home. Three picks, Sep through October. Usually get about **125 kg of lint per mu** (250 jin). Last year was like that, year before too.

---

**Winter wheat (4.9 mu) — already in the ground**

Put it in mid-October last year. Nothing special for seed, just what the shop had — I don't save seed, the yield goes down if you do. Plowed in about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before drilling.

Now it's spring, wheat is greening up, looks okay. Time to topdress and irrigate. I'll spread urea at jointing — about half a bag per mu, so maybe 20 kg urea/mu, which is around 9 kg N. Add that to the base, I'm at roughly 15-16 kg N/mu on wheat.

Irrigate three times from the well — the winter watering in February if it was dry, one at jointing (soon), one at heading. One spray of herbicide for the wild oats and little grass weeds.

Hoping for **about 400 kg/mu** at harvest in early June. Last year 380, year before a bit more. Depends on if we get a hot dry spell at filling.

---

**Summer maize (4.9 mu) — follows the wheat**

Right after I cut the wheat in early June, I have to get maize in fast. Three, four days max, or I lose too much of the season. No time to plow properly. My nephew has a little two-row planter, he comes over, 30 yuan a mu, puts the seed and fertilizer in together. That's how everybody in the village does it now.

Seed is hybrid from the store, 30 yuan a mu. Compound fertilizer with the seed, about 20 kg/mu. Later in July when it's waist-high I'll topdress some urea, half a bag a mu.

Water once, maybe twice if it's dry. Sometimes I spray for the corn borer if the moths come thick. Not every year.

Harvest late September. Usually **450 kg/mu** of grain. Some we grind for flour, some goes to the pig.

---

**What I'm worried about**

Fertilizer prices keep going up. If they go up more this year I'll cut back a bit on the cotton topdress — can't spend what I don't have. The boys' money helps but I try not to lean on it. Weather is the other thing, can't do anything about it. If a big rain comes at cotton picking that's a bad year. If drought hits in May-June, we'll pump more and hope the well holds.
